15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: Once more, I took my seat next to Hugo in the middle of the House of Delegates.

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: My uncle seemed to be in a grim mood today. He watched with agitation as the representatives began filing into the room.

20.speaker: Hugo Toras
20.text: "Are you sure it's a good idea to be here today, Your Majesty? You have every right to shutter the House of Delegates while the war is ongoing."

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: My uncle watched with agitation as the representatives began filing into the room.

25.speaker: Hugo Toras
25.text: "Your first visit to the House of Delegates since the RPP took over as majority party."

26.speaker: Player_Romus
26.text: "And give my enemies in ATO more ammunition against me? Never."

27.speaker: Player_Romus
27.text: "I can't blindly fight a war without knowing what's going on in my country."

28.speaker: Player_Romus
28.text: "Failing to appease my citizens now will lead to mutiny down the line. You know that."

29.speaker: Hugo Toras
29.text: "I hope they behave themselves in front of their King."

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "No. It's not what Vina would have wanted."

34.speaker: Player_Romus
34.text: "Not as long as my daughter's lover is one of the speakers."

41.speaker: Hugo Toras
41.text: "I am truly sorry, Romus. But the hostage situation with Her Highness is all the more reason why..."

43.speaker: Narrator
43.text: My uncle watched with a smile as the representatives began filing into the room.
43.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Pales_War"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseElections_RPPWinsSeats"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseElections_RNCWinsSeats"] == true)

47.speaker: Hugo Toras
47.text: "I think we'll find a lot more supporters of the Crown since the last time we were here."

48.speaker: Hugo Toras
48.text: "I'm relieved that the RPP's historic gains six years ago were a mere anomaly."

49.speaker: Hugo Toras
49.text: "We appease them by winning. Which we actually might have a chance at, if we focus and apply ourselves."

50.speaker: Hugo Toras
50.text: "That's what the reports from your Council are for."

51.speaker: Hugo Toras
51.text: "Your enemies already have formed their opinions about monarchies. Keeping our symbolic parliament open is not going to change them."

52.speaker: Hugo Toras
52.text: "Of course, the Delegates' advice is invaluable in times of peace. But I just think that..."

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: Manus Sazon, positioned behind the House Speaker podium, carefully put the wooden mallet aside.

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: Daria de Rava, positioned behind the House Speaker podium, put the wooden mallet aside.

58.speaker: Narrator
58.text: My uncle watched calmly as the representatives began filing into the room.
58.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Pales_War"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseElections_RPPWinsSeats"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.HouseElections_RNCWinsSeats"] == true) == false)

60.speaker: Hugo Toras
60.text: "It's a relief that the RPP didn't manage to make any gains over last time."

65.speaker: Player_Romus
65.text: "Perhaps Manus Sazon's charisma is wearing off."

67.speaker: Hugo Toras
67.text: "Unfortunate that our minority speaker managed to retain his position."

68.speaker: Player_Romus
68.text: "Even if that wasn't the case, I'm under no obligation to take the party's advice."

69.speaker: Hugo Toras
69.text: "That's true. But we don't want them getting big ideas."

70.speaker: Player_Romus
70.text: "I wouldn't mind hearing a little more from the opposition."

71.speaker: Hugo Toras
71.text: "As long as Manus Sazon is still minority speaker, you will hear plenty."

75.speaker: Player_Romus
75.text: "They will if they want to keep their heads."

76.speaker: Player_Romus
76.text: "Their movement is undeniable now. Perhaps we should start listening to them."

80.speaker: Hugo Toras
80.text: "Throw them a scrap or two. But we can't let them have the whole roast."

81.speaker: Hugo Toras
81.text: "There's over 50 of them. Beheading that many politicians would be... well, I would rather not say 'satisfying', but..."

82.speaker: Player_Romus
82.text: "Don't worry about it. The party and I have an understanding."

84.speaker: Player_Romus
84.text: "If they want to throw a tantrum, I'll let them. They still don't have any real power."

86.speaker: Manus Sazon
86.text: "As the majority speaker of the House of Delegates, I hereby call this session to order."

88.speaker: Manus Sazon
88.text: "Thank you for coming in the middle of this turbulent time, Your Majesty."

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: Manus looked down at his podium with a slight frown.

97.speaker: Manus Sazon
97.text: "At His Majesty's request, Grand Wiseman Ignacius will open today's session with a short prayer."

98.speaker: Daria de Rava
98.text: "I call this meeting of the House of Delegates to order."

100.speaker: Daria de Rava
100.text: "Thank you for coming in the middle of this turbulent time, Your Majesty."

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: Daria looked down at her notes with a smile.

109.speaker: Daria de Rava
109.text: "At His Majesty's request, Grand Wiseman Ignacius will open today's session with a short prayer."

110.speaker: Narrator
110.text: All Delegates' eyes followed Sal as he rose from the back row of seats and slowly walked to the center of the room.

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: Standing between Manus and Daria, he opened his arms wide.

113.speaker: Sal Ignacius
113.text: "As we gather here today, we call upon the spirit of St. Wruhec and the guidance of the divine."

114.speaker: Sal Ignacius
114.text: "May the great Nur bestow upon us the clarity of mind and purity of intent necessary to serve our people with honor and integrity."

118.speaker: Sal Ignacius
118.text: "We pray for the day when swords can be sheathed and harmony restored, when our troops return to their homes, and peace reigns once more in our lands."

119.speaker: Sal Ignacius
119.text: "We pray for the courage to face our challenges, and the wisdom to choose paths that lead to prosperity and peace for our kingdom."

120.speaker: Sal Ignacius
120.text: "God bless this assembly, and God bless our sovereign king."

124.speaker: Player_Romus
124.text: "Wise words. May you all take them to heart."

125.speaker: Narrator
125.text: The Delegates murmured the word as well. Sal shuffled back to his seat.

126.speaker: Narrator
126.text: The Delegates solemnly applauded. Sal shuffled back to his seat.

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: The Delegates murmured "Halaita" as Sal shuffled back to his seat.

128.speaker: Narrator
128.text: Manus waited until the Grand Wiseman sat down before continuing.

132.speaker: Narrator
132.text: Daria waited until the Grand Wiseman sat down before continuing.

133.speaker: Manus Sazon
133.text: "Yes, thank you, Grand Wiseman. That was... enlightening."

134.speaker: Daria de Rava
134.text: "Yes, thank you, Grand Wiseman. We will not forget the role of God in these halls."

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: He flipped open a binder on his podium.

136.speaker: Narrator
136.text: She flipped open a binder on her podium.

143.speaker: Manus Sazon
143.text: "The first item on our agenda is an update on Zille."

144.speaker: Daria de Rava
144.text: "The first item on our agenda is an update on Zille."

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: Manus closed the binder and looked up.

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: Daria closed her binder and looked up.

158.speaker: Manus Sazon
158.text: "Unless, of course, His Majesty had any closing remarks."

159.speaker: Player_Romus
159.text: "I would like to ask Grand Wiseman Ignacius to conclude our session with a prayer."

160.speaker: Player_Romus
160.text: "In fact, I do. House Speaker Sazon, esteemed delegates..."

161.speaker: Player_Romus
161.text: "No, I do not. This is your space, not mine."

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: The Delegates were all listening closely to me.

164.speaker: Player_Romus
164.text: "I understand that the RPP now holds a delegate majority. However, that does not give you free rein to speak critically of your King."

168.speaker: Player_Romus
168.text: "I respect the criticism you have expressed today and will take it to heart."

169.speaker: Sal Ignacius
169.text: "It would be an honor, Your Majesty."

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: Once more, Sal walked over to stand between the two House speakers. This time, he took each one by the hand.

171.speaker: Sal Ignacius
171.text: "My beloved Delegates, do not let your differences prevent you from recognizing the Divine in each other."

172.speaker: Sal Ignacius
172.text: "Remember, we are but one people, watching over this kingdom by the great grace of our God, duty-bound to carry His truths into the mortal realm."

173.speaker: Player_Romus
173.text: "And the truths of His emissary, your sovereign king."

175.speaker: Player_Romus
175.text: "And yet, let us not forget that some of those truths are more truthful than others."

178.speaker: Narrator
178.text: Hugo and everyone else in the room repeated the word after me.

179.speaker: Player_Romus
179.text: "I thank you for bringing my attention to the plight of the less fortunate in my kingdom."

180.speaker: Player_Romus
180.text: "I tire of your constant negativity. The next time we convene in these chambers, I would like to hear only good news."

181.speaker: Player_Romus
181.text: "Do not forget that you are here to serve me. Not the other way around."

182.speaker: Player_Romus
182.text: "You can expect prompt action from the Crown regarding the matters you brought up today."

183.speaker: Player_Romus
183.text: "Even -- especially -- in the midst of war, we cannot neglect our internal welfare."

187.speaker: Player_Romus
187.text: "I will remind you that we are at war. And during a war, you stand behind your king no matter what."

191.speaker: Player_Romus
191.text: "No matter what is going on around us, we cannot neglect our internal welfare."

192.speaker: Player_Romus
192.text: "As members of one of the world's few remaining monarchist governments, I expect you to stand behind me no matter what."

193.speaker: Player_Romus
193.text: "It is by my sword you live. I could have this assembly dissolved at any moment."

197.speaker: Player_Romus
197.text: "I can serve my people a lot more easily when I am not surrounded by constant disagreement."

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "It is my hope that the majority and opposition can find common ground. Otherwise, we are all lost."

206.speaker: Player_Romus
206.text: "Thank you, and God bless our troops."

207.speaker: Player_Romus
207.text: "Thank you, and God bless you all."

208.speaker: Player_Romus
208.text: "I bid you farewell until next time."

209.speaker: Player_Romus
209.text: "Mr. Sazon, see you for dinner at ours next week."

214.speaker: Narrator
214.text: Hugo and the Delegates repeated the phrase.

215.speaker: Narrator
215.text: Hugo and the Delegates quietly repeated the phrase.

216.speaker: Narrator
216.text: The Delegates looked puzzled. A few applauded.

217.speaker: Narrator
217.text: Manus' face reddened. He nodded and left his podium.

219.speaker: Manus Sazon
219.text: "Then until next time, ladies and gentlemen."

221.speaker: Narrator
221.text: I repeated the phrase along with Hugo and the other Delegates.

222.speaker: Sal Ignacius
222.text: "It is not my wisdom, but that of the heavens above."

223.speaker: Narrator
223.text: My uncle and I remained seated as the session adjourned.

227.text: "I would like to ask Grand Wiseman Ignacius to conclude our session with a prayer."

290.speaker: Daria de Rava
290.text: "Then until next time, ladies and gentlemen."

291.speaker: Daria de Rava
291.text: "Unless, of course, His Majesty had any closing remarks."

292.speaker: Player_Romus
292.text: "Well. Seems like Rizia is doing better than ever."

301.speaker: Player_Romus
301.text: "So everybody loves me. That's a relief."

302.speaker: Hugo Toras
302.text: "To hear the Sazon boy tell it, yes. But do you trust him?"

303.speaker: Hugo Toras
303.text: "I would not put it so crassly."

304.speaker: Hugo Toras
304.text: "Be careful, Your Majesty. You cannot afford to fall into complacency."

305.speaker: Player_Romus
305.text: "House of Delegates? More like House of Irrelevance."

309.speaker: Player_Romus
309.text: "I'd better get to work passing decrees."

317.speaker: Hugo Toras
317.text: "Be careful how much you capitulate to the RPP. Their victory is already getting to Mr. Sazon's head."

318.speaker: Hugo Toras
318.text: "The RNC has some good proposals. But you needn't give Baroness de Rava everything she is asking for."

320.speaker: Hugo Toras
320.text: "I keep telling you, Your Majesty. Your presence is not required at these sessions."

322.speaker: Player_Romus
322.text: "Any thoughts on today's session, Your Grace?"

323.speaker: Hugo Toras
323.text: "The Sazon boy is getting overconfident since his election win. I would be careful of how much you capitulate to his party."

327.speaker: Narrator
327.text: He kept his eyes on the Delegates as they left the hall.

328.speaker: Hugo Toras
328.text: "Having said that... the concerns he raised about the public's discontent were valid. We should find a way to mollify them."

335.speaker: Hugo Toras
335.text: "The concerns he raised about public discontent were overblown, if you ask me. I would not worry about the state of the nation."

339.speaker: Hugo Toras
339.text: "And I don't trust his assessment of public opinion. The whispers I've been hearing tell a very different story."

340.speaker: Hugo Toras
340.text: "Having said that, I do trust his assessment of the public's opinion. It is consistent with what I've been hearing."

341.speaker: Hugo Toras
341.text: "Baroness de Rava is handling the House as capably as ever. But a certain opposition speaker is getting a little too confident for comfort."

342.speaker: Narrator
342.text: He kept his eyes on the Delegates as they left the hall.

343.speaker: Narrator
343.text: He picked up his attache case and paused to look at me.

344.speaker: Hugo Toras
344.text: "Having said that... the concerns raised about the public's discontent were valid. We should find a way to mollify them."

348.speaker: Hugo Toras
348.text: "The concerns that were raised about public discontent are overblown, if you ask me."

349.speaker: Player_Romus
349.text: "I know. I just felt like a good laugh."

350.speaker: Player_Romus
350.text: "I disagree. The Delegates need to be reminded whom they answer to."

351.speaker: Player_Romus
351.text: "I was kidding. It's always useful to hear how the public is doing."

352.speaker: Player_Romus
352.text: "You're absolutely right. I should listen to you more often."

353.speaker: Hugo Toras
353.text: "As long as you remember that what you're hearing may not reflect the truth."

354.speaker: Hugo Toras
354.text: "You have more pressing priorities than laughter, Your Majesty..."

355.speaker: Hugo Toras
355.text: "Ideally, my presence should serve as that reminder."

356.speaker: Hugo Toras
356.text: "I am your Grand Vizier. Trust me to fulfill my function."

357.speaker: Hugo Toras
357.text: "It's been a while since the two of us caught up. I hope you'll do me the honor of paying me a private visit once you're back from your trip to Derdia."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "If you have something to say to me, you should say it here."

359.speaker: Player_Romus
359.text: "As long as no wine is involved, I'd love to."

363.speaker: Player_Romus
363.text: "As long as wine is involved, I'd love to."

364.speaker: Player_Romus
364.text: "If the Derdians don't kill me? Sure thing."

365.speaker: Hugo Toras
365.text: "There are some matters that are best kept in the family."

366.speaker: Player_Romus
366.text: "The honor would be all mine, Your Grace."

369.speaker: Narrator
369.text: I stayed in my seat until the room was completely empty.

370.speaker: Narrator
370.text: Was Manus right? Was my public happy with my reign?

377.speaker: Narrator
377.text: And if he was, where would I go from here?

378.speaker: Narrator
378.text: Was Daria right? Was my public happy with my reign?

379.speaker: Narrator
379.text: And if she was, where would I go from here?

383.speaker: Narrator
383.text: Was Manus right? Was my public unhappy with my reign?

384.speaker: Narrator
384.text: And if he was, where would I go from here?

385.speaker: Narrator
385.text: Was Daria right? Was my public unhappy with my reign?

386.speaker: Narrator
386.text: And if she was, where would I go from here?

390.speaker: Player_Romus
390.text: "I can't promise you anything. Who knows if I'll make it back from Derdia alive."

394.speaker: Narrator
394.text: Daria forced a smile from behind the opposition podium.

396.speaker: Daria de Rava
396.text: "Yes. On behalf of both of our parties, your presence is much appreciated."

397.speaker: Narrator
397.text: She nodded at Manus, who flipped open a binder.

398.speaker: Narrator
398.text: Manus nodded his assent from his usual place behind the opposition podium.

428.text: "It's been a while since the two of us caught up. I hope you'll do me the honor of paying me a private visit one of these days."
